beats.narration_text: A scene can be a door, a character, or a whole level. Nodes supply capabilities. Saving their arrangement lets us reuse the object without rebuilding every part. Think of the scene as a reusable object boundary, not a synonym for level.

lecture.about: A scene is not necessarily a level
lecture.runner_up: A conceptual node diagram is useful after the actual definition
lecture.why: Official engine documentation grounds the term before a custom example

beats.narration_text: A scene is a reusable node tree, usually saved as a text scene file. One root owns this small example. A complete level, a player, a coin, and a menu can each be scenes.

lecture.why: Exact runnable source is the teaching target; a full editor layout would reduce usable code size.

beats.narration_text: Node itself has no position. Two D and three D spatial nodes provide transforms. Here a child keeps its local offset when its parent moves. Top-level settings and different node types can change that relationship.

lecture.why: The spatial or temporal transformation is the claim; a physical-object metaphor would obscure its exact geometry.

beats.narration_text: PackedScene holds a saved definition. Instantiate creates a live copy. These two copies have different positions, while resources inside them may still be shared. Independent nodes do not automatically mean independent materials or shapes.

lecture.why: Exact runnable source is the teaching target; a full editor layout would reduce usable code size.

beats.narration_text: The locked property is exported so each door instance can start with a different setting. Is open is runtime state. Both belong to the door script. The level can configure the public setting without reaching through the scene to manipulate private children.

lecture.about: Export a setting, preserve the boundary

lecture.why: Executed script exposes the configuration/state distinction directly

beats.narration_text: Two nodes can share the same Shape resource. Resize that shared resource and both boundaries change. Duplicate the resource when you need one independent boundary. This is resource ownership, separate from whether the nodes were instanced separately.

lecture.why: Exact runnable source is the teaching target; a full editor layout would reduce usable code size.

props.title: unique · source excerpt
props.code:
left.shape = shape
    right.shape = shape
    left.shape.size = Vector2(40,20)
    check("shared resize propagates",right.shape.size.x==40,right.shape.size)
    right.shape = right.shape.duplicate()
    right.shape.size = Vector2(10,20)
    check("duplicate isolates resize",left.shape.size.x==40,left.shape.size)

beats.narration_text: A level has a player and coins: composition. An inherited scene specializes a base scene: a variant relationship. Prefer exported settings over repeatedly exposing editable children. Reuse should preserve a clear boundary around the object.

beats.narration_text: Let the level connect a coin's collected signal to the score update. The coin reports what happened without locating a distant parent. Unique names help inside a scene; persistent state can live in an autoload.

beats.narration_text: The level creates two doors and connects the first door's approach signal. The door reports an actor; the level decides what that means for the level. No hard-coded chain of parent lookups is needed to find the recipient.

props.title: door-wiring · source excerpt
props.code:
var packed := load("res://door.tscn") as PackedScene
    var door := packed.instantiate()
    var other := packed.instantiate()
    door.position = Vector2(600,380)
    other.position = Vector2(1000,380)
    other.locked = false
    stage.add_child(door)
    stage.add_child(other)
    var p := walker(Vector2(350,380))
    var requests := [0]
    door.approach_requested.connect(func(_actor): requests[0] += 1)

beats.narration_text: A question block remembers whether it was used, so give it a small scene and an explicit state. Animate its visual child for a cosmetic bump. If the solid surface must push something, use an animatable body.

beats.narration_text: A fresh door starts closed. Opening one instance changes that instance's state and shape; it does not open its neighbor. If a door must remain unlocked across level changes, store that progression outside the disposable instance and restore it deliberately.

lecture.runner_up: A global-state diagram would introduce an unimplemented save system
lecture.why: Executed door state is a concrete example; persistence is explicitly a design extension

beats.narration_text: Keep actors, blocks, levels, interface, and layer definitions organized by responsibility. Test scenes in isolation. When editing text scenes, preserve resource references and existing identifiers; letting the engine save a PackedScene avoids hand-copying node identifiers.

lecture.why: Exact runnable source is the teaching target; a full editor layout would reduce usable code size.

beats.narration_text: Before an agent extends reference code, inspect the seed for old APIs, scaled collision nodes, hard-coded parent paths, and movement outside physics callbacks. Static searches are leads. A clean search does not prove behavior, and we have not audited an unseen course game.

lecture.why: Verbatim recorded output establishes the observation and keeps its evidence limits visible.
